name: Dynamic Alerts
author: Fadi Haddad

sections.description:
Dynamic Alerts creates multiple configurable notification bars for WordPress. Display a bar in posts, pages, templates, or Elementor using one shortcode. Each bar now supports translations without duplicating the bar.

Features

  • Multiple independent bars with their own styling and display placement.
  • Language versions: Arabic, English, and custom codes such as fr, de, es, zh-hant.
  • Automatic front-end locale selection when Polylang or WPML is active; otherwise use WordPress locale.
  • Optional explicit language override per shortcode or Elementor widget.
  • Original messages preserved as a fallback; optional translation-specific fallback.
  • Separate text direction (RTL/LTR/auto) and animation movement direction.
  • Continuous moving ticker of messages, paused on hover or keyboard focus.
  • Reduced-motion accessibility support and appropriate text isolation for mixed scripts.
  • Add, remove, and reorder messages in each language; per-language link destinations.
  • Editor live text preview (static, does not emulate scrolling).
  • Optional Elementor widget, loaded only when Elementor is active.
  • Arabic translations (.po/.mo) and a gettext source template (.pot).

Translation and multilingual behavior

The language of the WordPress dashboard (plugin labels) is distinct from the language of a visitor-facing alert.
To serve different page languages, use Polylang or WPML, or specify lang=”en” / lang=”ar” in the shortcode. Without multilingual tooling, WordPress alone usually provides a single site-wide locale; language cannot be inferred reliably from every page URL.
Translation files bundled in a plugin do not automatically make the translation approved on translate.wordpress.org. Community approval is a separate process.

Shortcode

[dynamic_alert id=”123″]
[dynamic_alert id=”123″ lang=”ar”]
[dynamic_alert id=”123″ lang=”en”]

The old shortcode without lang remains valid. The bar must be enabled and published (editors may preview drafts).

Privacy

Dynamic Alerts does not transmit announcement content or collect personal data. Selecting Google Fonts may request font files from Google; choose the theme font to avoid that external request.
sections.installation:
1. Back up the site and database.
  2. Upload the ZIP via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin on a staging site.
  3. Choose Replace Current if upgrading an existing installation.
  4. Open Dynamic Alerts > Notification Bars and edit a bar.
  5. Set the original messages as fallback, then use the Languages and live preview box to add AR/EN and other translations.
  6. Publish the bar and insert the shortcode in a page.
sections.faq:
Will my existing bars be deleted?

No. Existing post IDs and _wpnb_items stay in place; new language variants are stored separately. Back up before upgrade regardless.

Is Elementor required?

No. The shortcode works in WordPress without Elementor. The optional Elementor widget is registered only if Elementor is active.

Can I use Polylang / WPML?

Yes. Dynamic Alerts reads the current front-end language from Polylang, then WPML, then WordPress locale. The content remains in a single alert bar.

Can I add a language other than Arabic and English?

Yes. Add a language code to the bar (such as fr or de), then provide the messages and optional links. User-facing display detects that code when the site language system exposes it or when specified in the shortcode.

What if a translation is empty?

The bar shows its configured fallback language, if populated, or its original messages.

Are these WordPress.org translations officially approved?

Not solely by installing this package. They must be submitted/reviewed in the WordPress.org Polyglots translation system.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • Added translation-specific texts and links for arbitrary supported language codes.
  • Added Polylang / WPML detection, shortcode language overrides, and fallback controls.
  • Added automatic RTL/LTR handling, mixed-script isolation, and independent movement direction.
  • Added add/remove/sort message controls, with a live editor preview.
  • Updated the ticker to a continuous moving group and improved reduced-motion behavior.
  • Added an optional Elementor widget for selecting any published alert bar.
  • Updated Arabic PO/MO and added POT for WordPress.org translation workflow.
  • Preserved old meta, bar IDs, shortcodes, and original design settings.
  • Avoided erasing original settings when an external editor omits the old metabox.

1.0.2

  • Improved per-bar authorization, unpublished-bar checks, CSS loading, and reduced-motion accessibility.

1.0.1

  • Multiple bars, shortcode support, typography and motion options, Arabic dashboard translation.
